svg.text: Consequences of special relativity, mass-energy and curved space-time
How the factors grow with speed
1/sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2): time t/t0 and mass m/m0

g.text: time dilation t = t0 / sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) (11.1)
length contraction l = l0 sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) (11.2)
mass variation m = m0 / sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) (11.3)
mass-energy E = m c^2 (11.4)
rest energy E0 = m0 c^2; K.E. = (m - m0) c^2; dm = dE/c^2
t0 (proper time) and l0 (proper length) are measured at rest relative to them
Ex 11.1: pendulum 3.0 s at rest, seen at 0.95c: t = 3.0/sqrt(1 - 0.9025) = 9.6 s
Ex 11.3: object at 0.8c: m = m0/sqrt(1 - 0.64) = 1.67 m0
a book opened in 1 s on a plane at 0.8c takes 1.7 s for an outside observer;
a 100 m train at 0.8c measures 60 m from the track; spaceship at c/2: 8 years
for the Earth, about 7 years for the crew; as v approaches c, m grows without
limit, so no material object can reach c
a heavy ball dents a stretched sheet: mass curves
space-time; bodies and light follow geodesics
no 'force of gravity': a body near a mass moves along a geodesic towards it

svg.text: Evidence: bending of starlight (1919) and gravitational waves

g.text: light from star A bends
as it passes the Sun; we
see the star at B, shifted
by phi; Einstein predicted
1.745 seconds of arc
(about 1.75 arcseconds),
confirmed in the 1919
solar eclipse
gravitational waves,
ripples in space-time,
detected in 2015 and
announced in 2016
